    16  /-!
    17  # Functions of bounded variation
    18  
    19  We study functions of bounded variation. In particular, we show that a bounded variation function
    20  is a difference of monotone functions, and differentiable almost everywhere. This implies that
    21  Lipschitz functions from the real line into finite-dimensional vector space are also differentiable
    22  almost everywhere.
    23  
    24  ## Main definitions and results
    25  
    26  * `eVariationOn f s` is the total variation of the function `f` on the set `s`, in `ℝ≥0∞`.
    27  * `BoundedVariationOn f s` registers that the variation of `f` on `s` is finite.
    28  * `LocallyBoundedVariationOn f s` registers that `f` has finite variation on any compact
    29    subinterval of `s`.
    30  * `variationOnFromTo f s a b` is the signed variation of `f` on `s ∩ Icc a b`, converted to `ℝ`.
    31  
    32  * `eVariationOn.Icc_add_Icc` states that the variation of `f` on `[a, c]` is the sum of its
    33    variations on `[a, b]` and `[b, c]`.
    34  * `LocallyBoundedVariationOn.exists_monotoneOn_sub_monotoneOn` proves that a function
    35    with locally bounded variation is the difference of two monotone functions.
    36  * `LipschitzWith.locallyBoundedVariationOn` shows that a Lipschitz function has locally
    37    bounded variation.
    38  
    39  We also give several variations around these results.
    40  
    41  ## Implementation
    42  
    43  We define the variation as an extended nonnegative real, to allow for infinite variation. This makes
    44  it possible to use the complete linear order structure of `ℝ≥0∞`. The proofs would be much
    45  more tedious with an `ℝ`-valued or `ℝ≥0`-valued variation, since one would always need to check
    46  that the sets one uses are nonempty and bounded above as these are only conditionally complete.
    47  -/
    48

    50  
"}]
